Senate Majority Leader John Thune says the GOP’s legislative agenda is giving people more money in their pockets on ‘My View with Lara Trump.’

Senate Majority Leader John Thune said Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer "lives in fear" of the Democratic Party's far-left wing Saturday on "My View with Lara Trump," arguing the longtime New York lawmaker has increasingly deferred to progressives as Republicans and Democrats head into the final stretch before the midterm elections.

"I think he lives in fear of that every day. I really do," Thune said when asked whether he thinks Schumer is concerned with being overtaken by "socialists."

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said he thinks Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., "lives in fear" of being overtaken by the Democratic Party's far-left flank. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon; (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite))

"I look at the way that the leaders in the Senate now act, and he voted once to open up the government when they were in the process of shutting it down the first time, and it just got blown up by the far left. And then ever since then, I mean, it's kind of whatever they want. They defer to that far-left base."

Thune made the remarks while discussing what he characterized as Democratic pushback in the Senate, arguing Republicans have been unable to advance several pieces of legislation that are traditionally supported by both parties, like military funding.

TED CRUZ NAMES ‘MOST POWERFUL DEMOCRAT’ AS HE WARNS SOCIALIST RISE HAS PARALYZED BIPARTISANSHIP

"We have a saying in my office that if you don't get national security right, the rest is conversation. You've got to protect the country. And so funding our military, the defense authorization bill, as I mentioned earlier — the Democrats blocked us from even getting on it on the floor. Historically, that's been bipartisan," Thune said.

He also emphasized the importance of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which he said is "critical to our intelligence community."

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, a Democrat from New York, speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Dec. 11, 2025. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Those are the kinds of things that keep me up at night. I think, to me, it's always about keeping this country safe and secure. Since that problem is kind of now solved, people are like, 'Okay, what have you done for me lately?' And obviously, you know, we've got more to do."

"But the trajectory that we are on as a country, when it comes to economic policy, national security, the border, all these issues, we are headed in the right direction," he added.

SENATE DEMS DRAW RARE LINE AGAINST MUST-PASS PENTAGON BILL

The South Dakota senator outlined Republicans' legislative priorities should the GOP retain control of Congress in November, which included military funding, judicial nominations, permitting reform and more.

"If we can maintain the majorities in the House and the Senate, the sky's the limit," he said.

Thune's remarks follow several prominent victories for Democratic socialist candidates, including recent wins in high-profile primary elections across state and local levels.
